explanation: The whole grid has `blockDim.x * gridDim.x` threads, so after each thread handles element `i`, the next element nobody has touched is `i + blockDim.x * gridDim.x`. Consecutive threads still touch consecutive addresses in every iteration, so the loop keeps coalescing. Interviewers like this pattern because it decouples the launch size from the problem size: you can size the grid to the hardware (say 4 blocks per SM) and reuse per-thread setup across iterations.
